headline: Oil crosses $96 on the first direct Houthi tanker strikes — PSX is shrugging it off so far, but refiners are the only names actually pricing it in.
summary: Brent crude has climbed three straight sessions to $96, driven by the first-ever direct Houthi missile strikes on Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea — a genuinely new escalation route, not just noise. Global markets are shrugging it off (the VIX actually fell) and PSX opened roughly flat too, but this market has sold off hard on similar headlines before even when the world stayed calm, so a quiet morning shouldn't be read as a green light. The clearest reaction so far sits in refiners (ATRL, NRL), already trending higher on the crude spike. Banks stay favoured into next week's rate decision; cement, fuel retailers, and exporters carry the most oil-shock risk.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: High-rate carry still works into the July 27 SBP decision — six-month T-bills are yielding below the policy rate, and a hold is the consensus call.

sectors.name: E&P (OGDC, PPL, MARI)
sectors.why: Direct beneficiaries of a sustained Brent move above $96, though the share prices haven't caught up to the story yet — all three are still below their 20- and 50-day averages.

sectors.name: Refining (ATRL, NRL, PRL)
sectors.why: The part of the oil complex actually reacting in price right now — ATRL and NRL are both trading above their key averages near recent highs; PRL has already run hard and looks stretched.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Domestic-demand business with low direct exposure to the oil-import bill, a defensive tilt while crude is volatile.

sectors.name: OMCs (PSO)
sectors.why: Daily fuel-price pass-through plus a weaker current-account backdrop means a sustained oil spike is a margin and circular-debt risk, not a windfall.

sectors.name: Cement (LUCK, BWCL)
sectors.why: Energy costs eat into margins — BWCL's own results out today show gross profit falling even before this fresh oil leg.

sectors.name: Textiles & exporters
sectors.why: The Red Sea shipping-route risk just went from theoretical to concrete now that tankers have actually been hit.

watchlist.angle: A proven technical trigger is live: an OBV volume-divergence signal with a 96.6% historical hit rate and +5.11% average return across 89 backtested trades (high confidence) — volume has been leading price higher. Fundamentals back it up (cheap P/E 6.33, 32% profit margin), and banking is the macro desk's favoured sector into next week's rate decision.
watchlist.risk: A broad oil-shock risk-off day, or a surprise at the MPC, can still drag a strong technical setup down with the tape.

watchlist.angle: The clearest live price reaction to today's oil story: ATRL is trading above both its 20- and 50-day averages, RSI 55, within about 2.5% of its 20-day high — refiners react to a crude spike faster than upstream E&Ps do. Valuation is cheap (P/E 4.55) against the market.
watchlist.risk: Refining margins are thin (net margin around 7%), and the whole move depends on the escalation holding — a ceasefire headline, a pattern seen repeatedly this month, could unwind it fast.

watchlist.angle: Fundamentals screen attractive — cheap (P/E 7.07), highly profitable (48% margin), an 11% dividend yield that's comfortably covered. The desk's backtest library shows multiple positive-expectancy setups on this name historically (an ADX/PDI expansion strategy with a 68% hit rate over 44 trades), and the price is holding up better than the rest of the oil complex today — down just over 1% and still close to its 20-day high on elevated volume.
watchlist.risk: No strategy is actively firing today — this is a watch, not a live setup — and it carries the same de-escalation risk as the rest of the oil trade.

watchlist.angle: Today's other big headline: FY26 profit up 7% with a Rs10/share dividend declared. But the desk's own digging into the filing shows the nine-month print was only +2% YoY with gross profit down 18% on rising costs — the full-year number was carried by associate income and lower financing charges, not the core cement business. Worth watching precisely because the headline and the substance don't match.
watchlist.risk: Cement is the macro desk's flagged avoid sector today on energy-cost sensitivity, and BWCL's own numbers are the evidence for that call — a dividend doesn't offset a core margin trend that's actually worsening.

watchlist.angle: A confirmed, dated catalyst: a Rs16/share dividend with book closure on August 3, on the back of H1 profit up 33% YoY and record deposits. Fundamentals screen attractive (fair P/E 7.7, 31% margin, a covered 6.75% yield), and banking is the favoured sector into next week's rate decision.
watchlist.risk: No live technical trigger here today — the case rests on fundamentals and the calendar, so a broad pullback could still weigh on the shares into the book-closure date.

catalysts.event: DCR book closure — confirmed Rs0.66/share dividend

LOTCHEM book closure — confirmed Rs1.50/share dividend
PBS July CPI release — first print to capture fuel-price pass-through from the current oil shock
UBL book closure — confirmed Rs16/share dividend
MARI results (unconfirmed scraped estimate — not yet verified against a primary filing)
ATRL, NRL and POL results (unconfirmed scraped estimates — not yet verified against primary filings)

risks: The escalation could deepen further — another direct tanker strike or a wider Red Sea blockade would widen the import bill and pressure the rupee, and could force the SBP's hand at Thursday's MPC even though a hold is the current consensus.

Global calm isn't a reliable signal for PSX — this market has sold off hard on similar Hormuz/Red Sea headlines before even when global indices and the VIX stayed quiet, so today's flat tape doesn't rule out a sharp domestic move.

SBP's reserve cushion hasn't been re-verified past the week ended July 10 ($17.2bn, down $1.2bn week-on-week) — if it has eroded further heading into the MPC, that's a real vulnerability the market hasn't priced in yet.
